messages:
maria.dev: Heads-up: ACME reported a big p95/p99 latency regression on hosted API starting ~09:10 UTC. I traced it to a spike in KV prefix cache misses for their prefixes. Link: https://observability/redwood/trace/abc123 :eyes:
aj_sre: What does the miss rate time-series look like? any recent deploys or config changes?
sylvia_rt: Miss rate for their customer prefix jumped from ~5% to ~72% around 09:08. Query: `sum(rate(kv_cache_misses_total{customer=\"acme\"}[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total{customer=\"acme\"}[5m]))` shows ~0.72.
maria.dev: I pulled a few request traces. The cache keys include a random request-id suffix now. Example from logs:
```
cache_key="prefix:acme:user:1234:rid=7f3a2b"
```
Previously keys were `prefix:acme:user:1234` (no rid).
aj_sre: That explains entropy. Who rolled the change that appended `rid` to cache keys?
matt_oncall: That was the instrumentation PR by telemetry team merged 2:1 deploys ago (PR #4527). The change was meant to help tracing but they accidentally used the full request id in the cache key. Deploy-bot: deployed frontend-service @ 09:02 UTC to cluster-3 (git sha: b4f7c2).
jordana_pm: ACME is heavily impacted — they escalated to support with screenshots showing 2–3x tail latency. We should prioritize mitigation.
aj_sre: Short-term mitigations: 1) rollback PR to remove rid from cache key 2) increase KV cache size for cluster-3 so eviction pressure drops 3) actively warm prefixes for ACME to reduce cold misses. Which is fastest?
matt_oncall: Rollback is the fastest but requires approval from telemetry team. I can coordinate rollback in next 15m. Increasing cache capacity is possible but may cause evictions elsewhere; need infra sign-off. Warmup script is quick: we can issue a batch of representative requests to populate KV prefix entries.
sylvia_rt: I can run a synthetic warmup targeted at ACME prefixes. Quick script: `for id in {1..500}; do curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer <$TOKEN>\" https://api.redwood/v1/generate -d '{"prefix":"acme:user:'$id'","prompt":"warmup"}'; done` — will populate keys.
aj_sre: Before doing any live warmup, ensure rate limits / quotas won't throttle and that warmup requests are routed to same cluster. Also mask sensitive customer data.
maria.dev: Repro steps for diagnostics (oncall / SRE):
1) Run miss-rate query for acme namespace (5m, 1m, 15m).
2) Pull recent config: `kubectl -n runtime get cm cache-config -o yaml` and check `cache_key_template`.
3) Check recent deploys: `gh pr list --state merged --author telemetry --search \"cache_key\" --json number,title`
4) Capture a few sample cache keys from logs: `jq -r .cache_key /var/log/runtime/*.log | sort | uniq -c | head -n 50`

matt_oncall: I ran step 2 — config shows `cache_key_template: \"prefix:{customer}:user:{uid}:rid={request_id}\"`. That needs changing.
jordana_pm: ACME CSM just asked for ETA. If rollback + warmup, can we get tail latencies down in ~30-45m?
aj_sre: If rollback approved now and we do an immediate warmup, I think 30–60m is realistic: rollback ~10–15m, warmup ~5–10m, cache stabilization ~15–35m depending on eviction.
matt_oncall: I'll open a rollback PR and ping telemetry lead. Also I'll add a temporary routing rule to steer ACME traffic to cluster-1 where miss rate stayed low (we have capacity there).
sylvia_rt: I'm starting the warmup run for IDs 1..200 now against cluster-3 with low QPS (10 r/s) to avoid overload. Monitoring in grafana: https://grafana/redwood/d/kv-cache.
deploy-bot: rollback request opened for telemetry PR #4527 by matt_oncall.
infra-bot: notice: cluster-1 has ~23% spare GPU capacity; reroute suggestion queued.
aj_sre: Post-mitigation followups: 1) Fix cache key generation to strip non-deterministic fields (request_id) — set key template to `prefix:{customer}:user:{uid}`. 2) Add unit test to ensure cache_key_template isn't populated with high-entropy fields. 3) Add alert: `kv_cache_miss_rate > 0.2 for 10m` per-customer. 4) Run a one-off telemetry job to scan other recent PRs for similar template changes.
maria.dev: Also need a customer-facing note for support: short explainer + steps taken. Jordan, can you draft?
jordana_pm: Will draft and share in #support-escalations. ETA 25m.
matt_oncall: Rollback approved by telemetry lead. Rolling back now. I'll post the rollback completion timestamp.
maria.dev: Thanks all. After rollback and warmup, keep an eye on p95/p99 for ACME and the global eviction rate. I'll follow-up in thread with graphs. :thumbsup:
aj_sre: Assigning action items: matt_oncall (rollback + routing), sylvia_rt (warmup + monitoring), jordana_pm (customer comms), aj_sre (postmortem & alerts).
maria.dev: Thread note: we should also consider normalizing cache key behavior in SDKs to prevent future accidental injection of request-scoped metadata.
